record.paper_title: THE DIFFUSE LIGHT OF THE UNIVERSE: On the microwave background before and after its discovery: open questions
record.context_brief: Distance and locality of the 3K radiation
record.original_question: At what distance, and with what spatial distribution of sources, is the observed 3 K microwave background actually produced? More specifically, is it only a very distant fossil background emitted in the early universe, or could it instead be a more universal radiation field produced partly or wholly locally and at long distances, given that its smooth blackbody spectrum does not itself provide a direct distance measurement?

evidence.quote: No direct distance measurement can therefore be performed. At a consequence, this radiation could actually be produced - for all or part - in any region of the universe.

The nature of diffuse radiation is therefore a much more open question than it seems a priori. Is it really only a very distant fossil background radiation or simply a more universal radiation, filling the entire space and produced both locally and at long distances?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
The cosmic microwave background (CMB) is observed as a highly isotropic electromagnetic radiation field with a near-perfect blackbody spectrum at temperature T ≈ 2.725 K. Because a thermal blackbody spectrum carries no intrinsic distance information (the spectral shape alone does not encode the redshift or location of the emitters), the spatial origin of this radiation cannot be inferred from its spectrum.

Formulate and answer the following question: at what distance(s) from the observer, and with what spatial distribution of emitting sources, is the observed 3 K microwave background actually produced? Specifically, determine whether the observed radiation must necessarily be a relic background emitted at a single cosmologically distant epoch (e.g., a thin "last scattering surface" in the early universe), or whether it could instead be — wholly or in part — a universal radiation field continuously produced and re-processed throughout space, including by relatively local sources at moderate distances. Provide quantitative bounds on the fraction of the observed CMB intensity that could originate from sources distributed at distances much smaller than the standard last-scattering distance, consistent with all current observational constraints (isotropy on the sky, blackbody spectrum, angular power spectrum of temperature anisotropies, polarization, and spectral distortions).
artifact.status_search_result: The standard cosmological model places the origin of the CMB at the surface of last scattering, with measurements fixing its distance and a thickness of about 19 Mpc to 0.1% precision. However, since a blackbody spectrum carries no direct distance information, the question of whether part of the observed 3 K background could have a more local or distributed origin is not closed by spectral data alone, and no quantitative observational bound that uniquely fixes all of the CMB intensity to the last-scattering surface (as opposed to a partial local component) appears to have been definitively established. The question is therefore best characterized as conceptually open, though strongly constrained by current data.

status_evidence.title: Cosmic microwave background - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Standard description of the CMB as relic radiation from the surface of last scattering at z≈1100.
status_evidence.claim: Mainstream cosmology attributes the CMB to a distant last-scattering surface.

status_evidence.title: Measuring the Duration of Last Scattering
status_evidence.snippet: Cosmological data enables a 0.1% measurement of the thickness of the surface of last scatter: 19 ± 0.065 Mpc.
status_evidence.claim: Modern measurements precisely characterize the assumed last-scattering surface, but assume a cosmological origin a priori.

status_evidence.title: Does standard cosmology really predict the cosmic microwave background?
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of the assumptions underlying the standard interpretation of the CMB.
status_evidence.claim: There is ongoing scholarly discussion about the assumptions underlying CMB origin claims.
